newsitem.title: EU: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR MARCH 17-DEC 31, 1997 (PAGE 1/10 - MARCH 17-19).
newsitem.headline: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR MARCH 17-DEC 31, 1997 (PAGE 1/10 - MARCH 17-19).

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
AMSTERDAM - The Netherlands hosts summit of European Union leaders (June 16-17).
MADRID - NATO holds summit to set the course for enlargement (July 8 and 9).
LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg hosts summit of European Union leaders (December 12-13).
MONDAY, MARCH 17
THE HAGUE - The Dutch presidency hosts conference on "Governance in the Euro-Mediterranean region" (To March 18).
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - ECOFIN Council meets (1000/0900 GMT):
Agenda includes:
- Convergence programme of Germany.
- Convergence programme of France.

- Court of Auditors President Bernhard Friedmann statement and draft recommendation on the discharge on the annual report of the Court of Auditors for 1995; Court of Auditors President Bernhard Friedmann presentation and draft Council statement of assurance.
- Preparation for stage 3 of EMU (including technical characteristics of euro coins).
- Taxation of energy products.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU farm ministers meet (To March 19).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commission presentation on fixing farm products and certain connected measures for 1997-98.
- Proposal for Council regulation:
- Establishing an identification and registration system for beef;
- On beef products and beef based products labelling.
- Proposal for Council regulation on Member States action programmes to control expenses under EAGGF, guarantee section.
- Proposal for Council regulation modifying Council regulation 1765/92 instituting a support system for arable crops producers.
- Proposal for Council regulation modifying oenological practices and treatment provisions of regulation 822/87 on the common organisation of wine market.
- Proposal for Council regulation modifying regulation 3448/93 fixing exchange regime applicable to certain processed goods.
- EU strategy on the trade of flowers.
- (possibly) Proposal for Council regulation modifying regulation 3813/92 on the unit of account and conversion rates to be applied in the framework of a common farm policy.
- State of play of negotiations with third countries for the conclusion of veterinary and plant health equivalency accords - Commission report.
- Adoption in Community languages of Council directive modifying and updating directive 64/432/EEC on sanitary police problems in intra-Community exchanges of animal species (beef and pigs).
- (possibly) Proposal for Council regulation opening Community tarriff quotas for barley under code NC 1003 00.
- (possibly) Proposal for Council regulation fixing measures and compensations on sensitive reevaluations affecting farm revenues.
BULGARIA (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner van den Broek leads EU mission to discuss financial help before a funding deal with the International Monetary Fund is in place.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EU and African, Caribbean and Pacific countries (ACP) hold joint assembly (1430/1330 GMT) (To March 18). European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles gives opening address.
Agenda also includes:
- Dutch Development Cooperation Minister Jan Pronk gives address.
- ACP Council Major General Sitiveni Rabuka gives address.
- World Bank official responsible for sustainable environmental and social development Ismail Serageldin gives address.
- Draft general report on the impact of the U.N. world conferences 1990-96 on cooperation between the Union and the ACP States under the Lome convention.
- The future of ACP-EU relations and the Commission green paper.
- Urban development in the ACP countries.
- Regional cooperation in ACP countries.
- Fisheries in ACP countries.
- Industrial development in the ACP countries.
- Refugees and displaced persons in the ACP countries in the context of humanitarian aid policy.
- The situation in Africa's Great Lakes Regions, in Somalia, Chad, Nigeria, Togo, Angola and Zambia.
- Relations between South Africa and the signatory states to the Lome convention.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "Redrawing the map of Europe" (1115/1215 GMT). Speaker is London School of Economics Senior Research Fellow Michael Emerson. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
TUESDAY, MARCH 18
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EU Farm Council continues.
Ministers hold structured dialogue with Central and Eastern European Countries (1000/0900 GMT), followed by lunch.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - ACP-EU joint assembly (second of two days). Closing news conference on the outcome of the meeting (1315/1215 GMT).

BRUSSELS - Management Global Information (MGI) holds conference on "Monetary Union and large firms - How to manage the euro project" (0900/0800 GMT) (To March 19). Discussions include: how to take into account the changeover to the euro both in business processes and information systems; key opportunities for corporate finance and treasury departments linked to the switchover to the euro. Venue: Hotel Le Meridien. Contact: MGI (33) 1 41 10 20 80.
BRUSSELS - European Business Aviation Association (EBAA) holds conference on "An uplift for business aviation" (1100/1000 GMT) (To March 20). Venue: Sodehotel. Contact: EBAA (322) 721 4272.
WEDNESDAY, MARCH 19
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner van den Broek communication on new guidelines for the PHARE programme in the framework of pre-membership.
- Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro communication on structuring and reducing support for ACP countries' debt.
- Commissioner Flynn communication on the second stage of the social partners' consultation on sexual harassment at work.
- Commissioner Bonino communication on consumer education and training.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (1430/1330 GMT) (To March 20).
Agenda includes:
- Employment, competitiveness and economic globalisation.
- Classification, packaging and labelling of dangerous preparations.
- Craft industries and small and medium sizes entreprises.
- The challenges facing the European defence related industry.
- Procedure for the provision of information in the field of technical standards and regulations.
- Annual report of the cohesion fund 1995.
- Amendments to basic decision relating to Socrates - Youth for Europe - Leonardo programmes to include Turkey among the beneficiary countries.
- European monitoring centre for racism and xenophobia.
- Collective redundancies.
- Community action programme "European voluntary service for young people".
- Relations between the EU and China.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP and Council Conciliation Committee meets on the directive on interconnection in telecoms (1845/1745 GMT). Venue: Justus Lipsius building.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Centre for Advanced Research in Economics (ECARE) holds academic session to celebrate its fifth anniversary (1600/1500 GMT). European Commissioner Monti gives address on the single market programme and European integration. Venue: Human Science library, avenue P. Heger. Contact: ECARE (322) 650 3075.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Packaging & Waste Law holds conference on "Packaging law in Europe" (To March 20). Venue: Sheraton Hotel. Contact: IBC Ltd (44) 1892 511 807.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "The BSE crisis and the EU" (1315/1215 GMT). Speaker is MEP Manuel Medina Ortega. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911. Commission approves merger in business travel services
EUROPEAN COMMISSION PRESS RELEASE: IP/97/204
DOCUMENT DATE: MARCH 11, 1997
The Commission approves merger in business travel services.

The European Commission has decided to approve an operation by which the Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits et du Tourisme S.A. and Carlson Companies Inc. acquire joint control of a new concentrative joint venture into which they merge their worldwide business travel operations, at present governed by the Union Agreement signed by them in 1994. CIWLT will also transfer its leisure travel business to the joint venture.

In view of the share that this joint venture will have in the travel markets concerned and the existence of significant competitors, the Commission considers that the proposed concentration does not create or strengthen a dominant position as a result of which effective competition would be significantly impeded in the EEA or any substantial part of that area.

The Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits et du Tourisme S.A. (CIWLT) belongs to the group Accor S.A. (France) which is operating a range of activities related to travel and business services including hotels, service vouchers, institutional catering, travel agencies, restaurants, railway services and car rental. Carlson Companies Inc. is active in the hotel and restaurant industries and operates travel agents, tour operators and other travel-related services. END OF DOCUMENT.
